name: African Peanut Stew
notes: Similar to tasty African food Denise and Mark found on their 2025 Newfoundland trip. Excellent served with brown rice. One recipe is enough for 6+, doubled, you can freeze some leftovers. This is a hearty meal—excellent with a fruit salad.

items: ½ tsp cayenne (reduce to half if you’re worried about spiciness–you can always add more at the end)
2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into ½-inch cubes (about 5 cups)

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.body: Cook **1 diced onion** and **1-2 tsp vegetable oil** in a large pot over medium heat until the onions are translucent.

steps.title: Add garlic and ginger
steps.body: Add **3-5 cloves minced garlic** and **1½ Tbsp finely grated fresh ginger** and cook until fragrant, 1-2 minutes.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.body: Stir in **1 Tbsp curry powder**, **½ Tbsp cumin** and **½ tsp cayenne** (reduce to half if you’re worried about spiciness–you can always add more at the end) and cook 1-2 minutes.

steps.title: Add tomato paste and peanut butter
steps.body: Stir into the pot until mixed in: **6 oz tomato paste** and **⅓ cup peanut butter**.

steps.title: Simmer the stew
steps.body: Add **28 oz diced tomatoes**, **2 large sweet potatoes**, peeled and cut into ½-inch cubes (about 5 cups), **1½ cups dry red lentils**, rinsed, and **3 cups vegetable broth** (or chicken broth). Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer for 15-20 minutes, until the lentils are fully cooked (turn to very low, and stir occasionally to prevent burning).

steps.title: Season
steps.body: Salt and pepper to taste, and add more cayenne if desired.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Ladle into large bowls, along with brown rice for a nice texture contrast, and top with cilantro.
